correctness.rationale: The DFT at M>=2n-1 splits all Hermitian modes into a square radial monomial Vandermonde and replicated narrower lag blocks. Lagrange inversion gives a norm-convergent rank-one inverse limit, with coefficient e^t S_n(t)B. Narrower offdiagonal blocks have strictly better collapse exponents, and the spectral maximum tends to e^-t H_n(t). A monic Chebyshev interpolation identity and weighted Cauchy prove B>=2^(n-2), including uniqueness of equality weights and nodes. Complete dimensional/norm factors checked against direct real Hermitian matrix SVD with 105 finite assertions; numerical evidence is supportive only.

value.rationale: Full finite-dimensional Husimi tomography near coalescing radii is a natural ill-conditioned measurement regime. The exact exponent n-1 and dimension-dependent coefficient distinguish the hardest diagonal radial information loss from offdiagonal modes, and the unique optimal allocation prescribes n circle locations and per-circle budgets. This quantitative stability/design law is more informative than rank or scalar regression alone; no broader finite-width or shot-noise claim is made.
